title: Iconic spooky North West doll Stumpy takes up residence at Chester's My Haunted Hotel
excerpt: A VENTRILOQUIST dummy called Stumpy, a spooky North West icon, is set for My Haunted Hotel in Chester.
content:
CHESTER is set to become home to a North West haunted icon from next week.

Stumpy is a ventriloquist doll whose story dates back to the 1970s in the North West of England.

He originally belonged to a one-armed man who regularly visited his local pub and entertained friends and customers with ventriloquist performances.

From Friday, he will “take up residence” at My Haunted Hotel in Lower Bridge Street, which staff are delighted about.

Harry Achilleos, from My Haunted Hotel, gave the background on how Stumpy has achieved his cult status over the years.

He said: “During these performances, Stumpy would apparently tease his owner about having only one arm.

“In response, the man would become frustrated, pull off Stumpy’s arm and throw it across the room, much to the amusement of everyone watching.

“However, according to the story, Stumpy didn’t take kindly to being laughed at and would begin heckling the audience instead of his owner.

“The performances were reportedly so convincing that some customers began questioning whether Stumpy was possessed, suggesting that the man wasn’t actually controlling him at all.

“Things took a more disturbing turn when members of the audience began reporting unexplained shooting pains in their arms.

“Interestingly, these experiences were said to affect only those who had laughed at Stumpy when his arm was removed.

“There is also a legend surrounding Stumpy’s original owner. It is said that he had once laughed at Stumpy himself and subsequently experienced the same shooting pain in his arm. Some believed this was connected to how he lost his arm and came to own Stumpy in the first place.

“Eventually, complaints from customers reportedly led to the man stopping his performances altogether.”

Even in retirement, Stumpy’s legacy is spooky, as Harry explained.

He said: “More recently, Stumpy was resident at Bygone Times in Chorley, a large antiques centre comprising seven warehouses filled with antiques and collectables from different vendors.

“Friends of the owners decided to showcase Stumpy and his unusual history within the allocated space of Charnock Richard Antiques in Warehouse 6.

“However, according to those who spent time around him, things were never quite the same after his arrival.

“Visitors began complaining of unexplained pains in their left arms, sometimes after interacting with Stumpy or making jokes about him.

“Objects were also reported to fall over unexpectedly in the area surrounding his display, without any obvious explanation.

“Perhaps one of the strangest occurrences involved Stumpy himself. There were occasions when he would apparently disappear from his usual display area, before eventually turning up again.

“These incidents became part of Stumpy’s growing reputation, with staff, vendors and visitors sharing accounts of unusual experiences associated with him.

“Over time, Warehouse 6 developed a reputation for strange occurrences, particularly around the area where Stumpy was displayed.”

Harry says he is looking forward to seeing how Stumpy “settles in”.

He added: “Given his unusual history and the experiences reported during his time at Bygone Times, he is a particularly interesting addition to the hotel.

“What makes Stumpy’s story so fascinating is that it spans several decades, from his original performances in the 1970s to the unexplained incidents reported by people who encountered him more recently.

“Whether people believe there is something paranormal about him or simply find his history intriguing, Stumpy certainly has a story that gets people talking.”
